sources.entry: dateparser - A Python parser for human-readable dates in over 200 language locales.

summary.one_liner: dateparser is a Python library that parses human-readable date strings in more than 200 language locales, including relative expressions like "two weeks ago" and timestamps.
summary.what_it_does: The library's main entry point is dateparser.parse(), which turns free-form date text into Python datetime objects. It handles absolute dates, relative dates ("in two months", "next Wednesday"), Unix timestamps, and timezone abbreviations or UTC offsets. Language is autodetected by default, or can be fixed with the languages argument, and date order (DMY/MDY/YMD) can be set explicitly. Settings control behaviour such as preferred past or future dates, default timezone, and handling of incomplete dates like "December 2015". It also has search_dates() for pulling dates out of longer text and time span detection for phrases like "past month". Optional extras add non-Gregorian calendars (Persian Jalali, Hijri, French Republican, Minguo).
use_cases: parsing dates scraped from web pages in multiple languages
converting relative phrases like '3 days ago' into real dates
normalizing mixed-format dates from CSV, PDF or log files
letting users search by natural date expressions
how_to_run: pip install dateparser[calendars]  # optional, for non-Gregorian calendars
notable: Parses dates in more than 200 language locales, with automatic language detection
Handles relative dates, timestamps, and timezone abbreviations or UTC offsets in one call
Search of dates within longer text via search_dates(), with time span detection such as 'past month'
Customizable through a settings dictionary (date order, preferred past or future, timezone, strict parsing)
Supports Persian Jalali, Hijri, French Republican and Minguo calendars via an optional extra
caveats: Date search in longer text is described in the README as limited and needing improvement
Ambiguous dates are not resolved by locale; date order must be set explicitly (e.g. DATE_ORDER) for UK/Australian-style DMY input
Non-Gregorian calendar support requires installing the optional calendars extra
keywords: turn '3 days ago' into a date
